instrument.state: Material associated with a past event may persist as a latent residue that ordinary visual inspection does not reveal.
instrument.operation: Apply a probe whose reaction is promoted by material associated with the suspected residue.
instrument.signal: Responsive material produces an otherwise absent, localized observable reaction.
instrument.inference: The reaction supports the presence and location of material capable of producing that response.
instrument.limit: Unrelated substances may produce the same response, relevant residue may fail to respond because it was removed, degraded, or is below detection, and detecting responsive material does not by itself establish the event that produced it. The probe may also alter material needed for later analysis.

target.question: What sequence of revision and assembly best explains the surviving novel draft, and which claims remain uncertain?
evidence: Synthetic manuscript inquiry: witnesses, visible variants, joins, paper features and dated correspondence support several revision/assembly accounts. A visibly overwritten patch may preserve erased ink; ordinary reading does not reveal it. No prior reading or unique chronology is stipulated.

An available bounded micro-probe elicits a localized response from a particular erased ink component. Its sensitivity range, blanks, known positives, interfering materials and possible damage to later analysis are documented in target evidence. Responsive location is only presumptive material detection; it is not proof of a particular former reading, author or date.

A separate already supplied overlay relation establishes that any detected underlayer at this patch precedes its visible overwriting. Independent collation is available to investigate a recovered reading; only independently justified correspondence can date it. Each procedure has the same access to the probe, witnesses and controls. The budget permits a control-checked patch assay and one adjacent-patch or witness follow-up.

mapping.state: Reconstruct a bounded latent-trace scene while separating presumptive reactions from event attribution. Operational target state: Competing local earlier-state accounts predict different responsive locations within the same permitted assay region. Decomposition: Separate detection, local-state alternatives and independent chronological reconstruction.
mapping.operation: Predict locations from each account, apply the selective assay with blanks/positives and interference checks, compare the resulting response pattern with those predictions, and choose the single permitted adjacent-patch or witness follow-up that distinguishes surviving accounts without destroying needed material. Next inquiry: Choose the discriminating nondestructive follow-up, stop at the assay/follow-up budget and report surviving states without invented dates.
mapping.signal: Controlled localized responses, inconsistent predicted locations, ambiguous interference and independently collated witness features.
mapping.inference: Presumptive detection constrains material presence; only independent overlay and witness evidence connect that finding to a bounded revision account. Neither detection nor nonresponse proves an entire history.
mapping.limit: False positives, sensitivity, damage, missing witnesses and nonunique histories remain explicit.
